project.name: dam-kemon-backend
project.description: Damkemon is a Bangladesh price-comparison backend that nightly indexes more than 60 e-commerce shops into MongoDB and serves fast catalog searches with cross-shop deduplication and grouped pricing. It is a Spring Boot 4 service on Java 17. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand the backend's purpose, operational guidance, and the broad areas it supports. It provides the context for the API, catalogue, data, security, and delivery layers visited next.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap
tour.description: The Spring application entry point is the runtime starting place for the backend, while the Gradle build configuration defines how that application is built and run. Together they establish the project boundary before following any business workflow.

tour.title: Runtime Security
tour.description: Runtime configuration and the security support files establish the environment-specific behavior and the request-processing security boundary. This is the foundation for every authenticated HTTP workflow introduced in the next step.
tour.languageLesson: YAML configuration keeps environment-dependent settings outside Java code. Spring profiles can layer deployment-specific values over common defaults, while secrets should be supplied by the runtime rather than committed to the repository.

tour.title: Account API
tour.description: The authentication and account controllers expose the HTTP-facing workflows for identity and account management. Building on the security boundary from Step 3, these controllers show where incoming requests enter the application layer.

tour.title: User Persistence
tour.description: The User domain model defines persisted user records, and its repository provides the Spring Data access boundary for those records. This pairs naturally with the account API because identity workflows need a durable source of user state.

tour.title: Catalogue Data Core
tour.description: Product and shop models are the most widely referenced persisted concepts in the graph, with repositories that centralize access to each collection. Understanding this data core explains why later search, controller, and indexing workflows converge on the same entities.

tour.title: Search Workflows
tour.description: The product controller and service present a high-scope route from HTTP requests to catalogue operations. Catalog search adds the dedicated search behavior on top of the product and shop data introduced in Step 6.

tour.title: Catalogue Indexing
tour.description: Bulk indexing is a broad integration point for the backend's catalogue discovery and ingestion work. The scraper product representation and extractor contract clarify the handoff from external collection to the persisted catalogue core from Step 6.

tour.title: Deployment Automation
tour.description: The staging and production configuration files separate environment behavior, while the deployment workflows automate delivery for each target. This closes the tour by showing how the application and its security requirements become an operated service.
tour.languageLesson: CI/CD YAML expresses event triggers, jobs, and ordered steps. Separate staging and production workflows make it possible to validate an artifact in a lower-risk environment before releasing it to the production runtime.
